key_concepts: Weathering is the breaking of rocks into fragments without moving them to a new location.
Mechanical weathering breaks rocks without changing their chemical nature.
Chemical weathering changes the composition of rocks.
Water, wind, temperature, plants, animals, and people act as agents of weathering.
Weathering helps shape Earth's surface and forms soil and landforms.
Erosion is the movement of rock fragments and soil from one place to another.
Sediments are the materials transported by erosion.
Water, wind, animals, and humans are agents of soil erosion.
Too much soil erosion makes soil dry, coarse, and unable to hold water for vegetation.
Eroded sediments can clog irrigation systems and reduce plant water supply.
Soil erosion reduces food production and affects animals and humans.
Soil erosion can be controlled through natural vegetation, contour plowing, strip cropping
